summary: Redwood AE/SE walked the Findable search team through hosted embeddings + reranker endpoints. Discussed integration patterns (embedding store + reranker), latency vs cost tradeoffs, security/compliance (SOC2/KMS/VPC options), and next steps to run benchmarks on their query set. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-09 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 49m
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Maya (Findable Head of Search), Evan (Findable Sr. ML Eng), Samir (CTO)
Shared artifacts: Demo deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/embeddings-rerank.pdf), Benchmark script link (shared in chat), Security whitepaper (will share)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, hi, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, AE on the Redwood inference team, with Leo and Priya. Quick agenda: walk through hosted embeddings + reranker flow, show live demo on the console and API, answer security questions, and outline pilot next steps. Maya, you wanna kick off with a bit of context on Findable's current setup?

[00:28] Maya: Yeah sure, thanks. So quick background — we run a hybrid search stack today, core doc store in Elasticsearch, vector store using Pinecone for semantic matches. We do a two-stage search: embed+ann then a reranker model in-house to reorder results. Pain points: reranker latency spikes, cost complexity across infra, and occasional relevance regressions after model updates. We're exploring hosted solutions to simplify infra and try to bring down tail latency.

[01:10] Ava: Got it, thanks. Evan, what's your typical QPS and latency targets?

[01:16] Evan: Typical QPS about 120 during peak, p95 end-to-end under 200ms is the goal — ideally under 150ms for front-line results. For reranker we tolerate slightly higher but want predictable SLOs. Also SLOs for token cost since we're aggressively optimizing spend.

[01:40] Leo: Cool — that maps to what we see with similar customers. Today I'll demo Redwood's hosted flow: embeddings endpoint for vector generation, storing vectors in your store (we show an example using Pinecone/FAISS), then a hosted reranker endpoint that calls the embed+rerank combo. We also have the Redwood Console for per-model latency, token breakdown, and Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization.

[02:15] Priya: Quick note — we have pre-tuned reranker models (we call them rerank-lite and rerank-pro) optimized for latency vs quality tradeoffs. We'll show both.

[02:35] [Demo start — screen share]
[02:40] Leo: Alright I'm on the console — top right is the model catalog. For hosted embeddings we expose a /v1/embeddings endpoint, payload is simple: {"input":"..."}. Here's a quick curl example in the chat.

[03:05] Speaker 1 (auto): "curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{\"input\": \"how to reset password\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"

[03:20] Leo: The response returns a vector — length depends on model; default is 1536 for our 'rb-embed-1536' model. You can also request lower dimensional embeddings for cost efficiency. We recommend 1024 or 768 if you have strict storage budgets.

[03:52] Maya: Wait, how lossy is the lower-dim option? We saw some drift with a 512-dim compressed model at Pinecone.

[04:00] Leo: Totally — there is a tradeoff. Our Optimize module runs an evaluation on your holdout and can recommend quantization/dimensions with expected recall and MRR deltas. For small query sets, we typically see <2% MRR drop going 1536->768 for conversational re-ranking tasks, but depends on corpus. We'll run that during the pilot.

[04:32] Ava: On storage — you can keep vectors in your store (e.g., Pinecone) or use Redwood's optional managed vector store. For hosted API customers many keep their own vector store for compliance reasons.

[04:50] Samir: About compliance — we need SOC 2 and KMS integration. Also data residency for EU customers, and ability to purge.

[05:02] Priya: We support SOC 2, have KMS integrations yes — we'll send the whitepaper. For private deployments we have VPC options and on-prem packages but for this pilot hosted with KMS and retention controls usually suffices.

[05:25] Leo: Jumping to reranker: two patterns — client-side rerank (pull top-k from vector store and call Redwood rerank endpoint with candidate docs + query) or server-side rerank where Redwood can accept a candidate payload and return ranked ids. Example: you call /v1/rerank with {query, candidates:[{id,text,metadata}, ...]}. We return a scored list with normalized scores plus explanations if you enable the debug flag.

[06:05] Evan: How big can candidates be? We typically send top-50 candidates.

[06:10] Leo: Top-50 is fine; payload size matters for latency. We recommend sending text chunks limited to ~4k tokens total in the candidate field for fastest p95. For long docs we chunk upstream.

[06:28] [08:00] Maya: Do you support rerank-by-embedding similarity + learned reranker? Like hybrid scoring?

[08:06] Leo: Yes — you can combine vector similarity score with reranker score. In the API you get raw scores so you can implement weighted combos or use our built-in hybrid scorer which supports weight tuning in the Console.

[08:30] [Demo — live call example]
[08:34] Leo: I'm going to run a sample q: "best way to onboard users". First we call embeddings endpoint for the query, then ANN search on host store, then call reranker. Watch latency numbers here: embedding call is ~12ms, ANN lookup depends on your store — here Pinecone returns in ~35ms, rerank call is 68ms. Total ~120ms in demo environment.

[09:20] Maya: Those are promising numbers. Our production ANN is 40-60ms. Reranker at 68ms seems reasonable. Is that the rerank-pro model?

[09:27] Leo: That's rerank-pro on an optimized kernel with aggressive batching disabled. If you accept a little more latency we can get +4% MRR with rerank-pro vs rerank-lite.

[09:50] Evan: Batching — how do you recommend batching for user-facing queries? We worry about head-of-line blocking.

[09:58] Priya: Optimize recommends dynamic batching thresholds based on latency SLOs. You can set max latency and it will auto-batch until that threshold. For low-latency front-line we often disable batching and use caching; for background reranking jobs batching is enabled.

[10:25] Leo: Also prefix/KV caching helps: repeated conversational prefixes don't recompute the full transformer pass. For static rerank inputs caching probably less useful but for multi-turn it helps a lot.

[10:50] [11:30] Maya: Pricing — ballpark for hosted rerank? We're trying to compare to Pinecone + self-hosted reranker infra costs.

[11:38] Ava: Ballpark: embeddings $X per 1k (we put exact in proposal) and reranker charged per request (tokens processed). We also have committed Dedicated plans if you need capacity predictability. I'll put a detailed cost comparison in the pilot proposal.

[12:05] Samir: Does Redwood store any PII or raw text on hosted? We need to ensure data retention windows and purge on demand.

[12:14] Priya: By default hosted API processes request and doesn't persist input unless you opt into logging for debugging. We provide controls to disable logging, and support deletion requests and retention windows. KMS for encryption at rest is available.

[12:38] [13:00] Leo: Back to demo — console view: here's the per-route latency heatmap, token breakdown, and Optimize suggestions. Optimize suggested lowering sequence length on some calls and trying 1-bit quantization for rerank-pro in staging to drop memory without big QPS impact.

[13:40] Evan: Is quantization something you do transparently or we have to change model?

[13:44] Leo: We provide pre-quantized variants and a recommendation engine. You choose in the Console; we run evals and show expected recall/latency tradeoffs.

[14:05] [15:00] Maya: For the pilot we want a test harness that runs our historical queries and returns MRR, P@1, latency. Can Redwood run that or do we run locally?

[15:10] Leo: We do both — we provide a benchmark script (shared in chat) you can run locally, and we can run a Redwood-hosted job if you share logs and grant access. We'll compare to your baseline and give concrete Optimize suggestions.

[15:40] [17:20] Demo continues: Leo shows reranker config JSON and debugging output with token counts and per-candidate scores. There are a few minor transcription glitches here where model names show as "redwood infer" in the console label.

[18:10] Evan: Slightly off-topic — can we A/B test rerank-pro against our current reranker to measure delta?

[18:16] Priya: Yes, we support rollout rules in the Console for canary/A-B and automatic fallback. You can route X% of traffic to Redwood reranker and measure metrics in the dashboard.

[18:40] Maya: Any limits on concurrency for hosted? QPS 120 looks moderate but what about bursts?

[18:48] Ava: Hosted has burst capacity; for predictable needs we recommend Dedicated. For the pilot it's common to start hosted and then move to Dedicated if predictability is required.

[19:10] [21:00] Security deep-dive: Evan asked about SSO, audit logs. Priya: we support SAML/SSO integrations, RBAC, audit logs with retention policies. We send SOC2 report and details on how audit logs surface in the Console.

[21:40] Maya: One more question on latency: what portion of rerank latency is model vs network? If we host closer to our users will that help?

[21:50] Leo: Both matter. Model kernel and sequence length drive compute time; network round-trip adds overhead. For EU traffic, using EU-hosted endpoints drops RTT significantly. We can route by region.

[22:20] [24:00] Customer objection: concern about vendor lock-in and ability to move models on-prem later.

[24:10] Ava: We design for portability — same API and config across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. If you need on-prem we can do a private deployment or provide an exportable reranker configuration and model artifacts where allowed.

[24:40] Evan: Anything about model updates — how do you avoid regressions after a reranker model push?

[24:46] Priya: We have pre-deploy evals and can run your holdout test suite. Also rollout controls and automatic rollback if quality dips beyond thresholds you set in the Console.

[25:10] [27:00] Live Q&A: Leo runs a quick sample: compares rerank-lite vs rerank-pro on a small holdout and shows MRR numbers in Console (rerank-pro +3.8% MRR, p95 latency +22ms).

[27:50] Maya: That delta is attractive. If p95 is still within our threshold that's good.

[28:10] Ava: Next steps proposal: 6-week pilot, we provision a trial API key, ingest sample data, run benchmark, weekly check-ins, plan for dedicated if needed.

[28:35] [30:00] Samir: Financial approvals — we'll need a one-page SOW and estimate to route internally.

[30:10] Ava: Will do. I'll attach a pilot SOW and pricing.

[30:30] Evan: Integration question — do you have SDKs for Node/Python?

[30:36] Leo: Yes — Python and Node SDKs, and a small Java client. Demo code in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (link in chat).

[31:00] Maya: For our logging requirements we need to mask PII upstream. Can Redwood accept pre-masked payloads and still rerank?

[31:10] Priya: Yes, as long as the masked text preserves enough signal. We can also run a small eval to measure impact.

[31:40] [33:00] A brief cross-talk, filler: "uh-huh", "yeah", some audio overlap; minor transcription errors where 'KV cache' appears as 'K V cash' in automated text.

[33:30] Leo: Final checklist for pilot: sample logs + queries (Evan), pilot SOW sign (Samir), security questionnaire if needed (Maya), schedule bench run (Ava/Leo).

[34:05] Maya: We'll aim to send logs by 2/10.

[34:15] Evan: Yep I'll export top 50k queries and a 1k holdout set.

[34:25] Samir: Finance will want the SOW by 2/11.

[34:35] Ava: Great. We'll send the SOW and security docs by Thursday.

[35:00] [38:00] Closing — Alice? (typo) No, just wrapping up.

[38:10] Priya: Quick note — I'll include notes on Optimize recommendations and the expected MRR/latency impact for the two rerank variants in the follow-up.

[38:30] Maya: Cool. Thanks everyone.

[38:45] Ava: Thanks all. Recap in chat and we'll follow up with the pilot proposal and security bundle.

[39:00] [End meeting]

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mislabels (Speaker 1), minor word swaps, and automated tokenization quirks (K V cache).
